notes: Proceedings volume with several high-value sections for economic mechanisms and evidence around Roman 'crisis' and long-run decline. Core material includes Jongman on economic growth/decline using archaeological proxies and living-standard indicators, Nappo on Red Sea/East trade contraction and inflation/currency instability in the later 3rd century, and Verboven on debasement, exchange rates, and banking/frictions in the 'demise' of the Augustan monetary system. Also contains useful (though earlier) fiscal-background sections on western provincial taxation and contextual discussion of the Antonine plague.
